answer.summary: Winters says Eventbrite makes creator marketing easy by default—automating Facebook ad targeting and creative with its data—while offering an on-ramp for creators who want more control. This reflects “perceived simplicity”: advanced features are discoverable when sought, but unobtrusive for users who do not need them.

sections.heading: Simple by default, with a path to more control
sections.content: Event creators are often not professional marketers, so the Facebook advertising tool can handle targeting and creative for them. Creators who want to optimize their own audience segments and creative can use an on-ramp to do more themselves. Winters says this serves both kinds of users, though Eventbrite had not perfected the approach.

sections.heading: The broader design principle
sections.content: Winters calls the aspiration “perceived simplicity”: advanced features should be easy to find when a creator looks for them, but effectively hidden otherwise, so complexity does not burden users who do not need it. He notes creators range from people running a first, small event to experienced organizers running many events, and can become more sophisticated over time; fixed segmentation or exposing advanced functionality to everyone may not fit that range.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately says the default handles targeting and creative for creators who want it done for them, while an on-ramp lets others optimize those themselves. It also correctly connects this to perceived simplicity and cites supporting context. It makes no unsupported claim that information is missing.
